problems.reason: The age ranges for the oldest Lagerpeton fossils (241.464–237 Ma) contradict the radiometric dating of the Chañares Formation (236–234 Ma).
Both sentences state that the leaping hypothesis is debated and that the small pelvic girdle and reduced toes could indicate a running lifestyle.

notes: - contradiction: "The oldest Lagerpeton fossils date to the Upper Middle Triassic (Ladinian) period and were found in Gondwana, part of southern Pangaea, living between 241.464 and 237 million years ago." / "Radiometric dating places the Chañares Formation and its fossils between 236 and 234 million years old.": The age ranges for the oldest Lagerpeton fossils (241.464–237 Ma) contradict the radiometric dating of the Chañares Formation (236–234 Ma).
